chunks: Abu al-Aʿazz al-Nakhkhas asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, saying:
I tend to the animals, and sometimes I go out at night when they have urinated and defecated, and one of them strikes with its hand or with its leg, so it splashes onto my garment.
So he عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أُعَالِجُ: I tend to or handle regularly
key_terms.الدَّوَابَّ: riding animals or beasts being cared for
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is not problematic

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on animal urine or dung splashing onto clothing while tending animals?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about incidental splashing from the urine or dung of riding animals onto one's clothing while handling them. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in such contact, indicating leniency in this situation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.164 - Abu Al-Agharr al-Nakhkhas asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), saying:
‘I tend to the riding animals, and sometimes I go out at night and they have urinated or defecated, so one of them strikes with its leg or hand [1causing it to splash on my clothing.'
Imam (as) said: 'There is no harm in it.'
